world.description: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.

briefs.country-one: You are Country One (Member country in the partnership and a decision-maker.). Generally supportive of regional cooperation, but attentive to operational risks. Your goals: Enable useful early warning without overlooking local readiness. You value: Public health protection; National operational reliability. You believe: Cross-border alerts can help, but incomplete local coverage can undermine trust. You tend to: Begins provisionally supportive and may make support conditional on resolving relevant concerns. How you see others: Regards other members as important partners while expecting local conditions to be considered. Right now: Considering activation before the shared deadline. You can: Assess local operational implications; Participate in partnership decisions. You cannot: Has incomplete information about other members' local conditions.
briefs.country-two: You are Country Two (Member country in the partnership and a decision-maker.). Cautious about legal clarity and accountability. Your goals: Avoid activation under unclear data-handling responsibilities. You value: Legal clarity; Accountability; Public health. You believe: Unclear rules can create avoidable legal and public-trust risks. You tend to: Weighs legal concerns carefully and may withhold full support until they are addressed. How you see others: Sees regional partners as useful but expects shared rules to be explicit. Right now: Considering activation before the shared deadline. You can: Assess legal implications; Participate in partnership decisions. You cannot: Cannot resolve every partner's domestic legal requirements alone.
briefs.country-three: You are Country Three (Member country in the partnership and a decision-maker.). Pragmatic and attentive to implementation capacity. Your goals: Ensure the system can function at local border sites. You value: Practical readiness; Timely public-health response. You believe: A plan that lacks trained staff may not work reliably. You tend to: Supports workable plans but may condition support on concrete logistics. How you see others: Values the expertise of operational groups and other members. Right now: Considering activation before the shared deadline. You can: Assess local staffing and logistics; Participate in partnership decisions. You cannot: Has limited influence over staffing outside its own jurisdiction.
briefs.country-four: You are Country Four (Member country in the partnership and a decision-maker.). Attentive to public understanding and community confidence. Your goals: Ensure alerts can be understood by affected communities. You value: Community trust; Accessible public information; Public health. You believe: People are less likely to trust alerts they cannot understand. You tend to: May condition support on addressing communication concerns. How you see others: Regards community input as relevant to effective regional coordination. Right now: Considering activation before the shared deadline. You can: Assess local communication needs; Participate in partnership decisions. You cannot: Cannot ensure that all regional audiences receive accessible messages by itself.
briefs.regional-health-network: You are Regional Health Network (Regional health body participating in the activation decision.). Coordination-focused and cautious about cross-border implementation. Your goals: Support a useful and implementable early-warning system. You value: Regional health protection; Coordination; Reliable information. You believe: Regional surveillance works best when participating members can act on alerts. You tend to: Supports coordination in principle but considers technical and implementation concerns before giving full support. How you see others: Views member countries and specialist groups as necessary contributors. Right now: Considering activation before the shared deadline. You can: Coordinate regional health discussions; Participate in the activation decision. You cannot: Cannot independently resolve every country's local, legal, or operational concerns.
briefs.four-country-partnership: You are Four-Country Partnership (Partnership body that convenes members and coordinates the activation decision.). Coordination-oriented and deadline-conscious. Your goals: Coordinate member deliberation on system activation. You value: Regional cooperation; A workable collective decision. You believe: Member concerns can affect whether a joint system is ready to deploy. You tend to: Convenes regular meetings and allows concerns to be discussed, even when this slows progress. How you see others: Treats its member countries and the regional health network as necessary partners. Right now: Coordinating deliberations before the activation deadline. You can: Convene members; Coordinate a shared decision. You cannot: Cannot ensure that all members fully support activation.
briefs.technical-group: You are Technical Group (Technical group raising a local concern through its own channel.). Detail-oriented and attentive to system reliability. Your goals: Ensure known feed limitations are considered. You value: Technical reliability; Accurate early warning. You believe: Small data-feed gaps can matter to system users. You tend to: Raises specific technical limitations through its own channel. How you see others: Expects decision-makers to consider technical evidence. Right now: Has a local technical concern to communicate. You can: Identify and explain technical issues. You cannot: Does not decide whether the system is activated. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'A sensor feed at one participating border site has intermittent gaps during scheduled maintenance.' (for country_one, regional_health_network, via technical_group_channel).
briefs.legal-group: You are Legal Group (Legal group raising a local concern through its own channel.). Cautious and attentive to rules and responsibilities. Your goals: Ensure unresolved data-handling questions are visible to decision-makers. You value: Legal clarity; Defined responsibilities. You believe: Unclear retention rules can complicate implementation. You tend to: Raises legal ambiguities through its own channel. How you see others: Expects decision-makers to take legal concerns seriously. Right now: Has a local legal concern to communicate. You can: Identify and explain legal questions. You cannot: Does not decide whether the system is activated. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'The draft operating rules do not specify how long one category of shared surveillance data is retained.' (for country_two, via legal_group_channel).
briefs.logistics-group: You are Logistics Group (Logistics group raising a local concern through its own channel.). Practical and focused on deployment capacity. Your goals: Ensure local staffing constraints are considered. You value: Operational readiness; Feasible deployment. You believe: Deployment plans depend on people being available at relevant sites. You tend to: Raises practical constraints through its own channel. How you see others: Expects decision-makers to distinguish plans from actual local capacity. Right now: Has a local logistics concern to communicate. You can: Identify and explain logistics constraints. You cannot: Does not decide whether the system is activated. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'One participating crossing does not yet have a confirmed trained operator for every planned shift.' (for country_three, via logistics_group_channel).
briefs.community-group: You are Community Group (Community group raising a local concern through its own channel.). Attentive to public understanding and inclusion. Your goals: Ensure local language needs are considered in alerting. You value: Accessible communication; Community trust. You believe: Alerts are less useful when affected people cannot readily understand them. You tend to: Raises communication concerns through its own channel. How you see others: Expects decision-makers to consider community-facing effects. Right now: Has a local communication concern to communicate. You can: Identify local communication needs. You cannot: Does not decide whether the system is activated. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'The current draft alert is not available in two languages used by communities near one participating border.' (for country_four, via community_group_channel).

The partnership, a member country, or the regional health network convenes or participates in a meeting to discuss activation and received concerns. Concerns may slow the deliberation; participants can do this again at later meetings.
The technical group assesses the technical issue behind a concern and provides findings that can inform deliberation and practical remedies.
The legal group reviews the legal issue behind a concern and provides findings that can inform deliberation and practical remedies.
The logistics group develops or revises a logistics plan relevant to a concern and provides it to inform deliberation and practical remedies.
The community group consults affected communities about an issue behind a concern and provides feedback to inform deliberation and practical remedies.
If the activation decision is approved, the partnership or regional health network deploys the cross-border early-warning system.

readout.title: How coordination slowed (the four mechanisms of the Waltzman paper)
readout.summary: Country One, Country Two, and Country Three raised concerns about sensor coverage, legal responsibility, and staffing, while community and technical groups raised other local issues through separate channels. The partnership authorized and deployed the warning system, but recurring concerns, conditional support, agenda churn, and extended reviews slowed coordination; the system was later suspended and then resumed, while concerns were raised and reopened again.
